title: Can a robot camera calibrate itself without a checkerboard, and does it know when it is wrong?
lede: research programme on target-free camera self-calibration on two real cameras: bundle adjustment with the board's geometry withheld lands within 0.15% and 0.24% of Zhang's focal length and shows the board itself bends; over 560 converged view-subset solves the spread of view angles predicts the error (ρ −0.46/−0.58), the solver's σ is about 2× too small (2.4× near the critical set, where Zhang's is 5.8×), and a 0.5% σ gate rejects 92% of bad updates but accepts only 84% of good ones; the 2× is real (rms z 2.28 against the target-free solution), and a leave-one-view-out jackknife σ is honest with no fitted factor (rms z 0.70/0.65) but ranks good and bad updates worse (AUC 0.75 against 0.91); a released-object (bend-aware) Zhang equals target-free BA exactly, and adding k2 leaves σ overconfident (nested rms z 3.01); the 11×11 cornerSubPix window misplaces outer corners by up to 6.4 px, which made most of the apparent 5–9 px flat-board c_y shift (1.2–1.4 px with findChessboardCornersSB), moves Zhang's f by up to 1.3% between OpenCV detectors, and cleaner corners make σ less honest (nested rms z 3.1–3.5)
summary: A research programme (proposal and log on the project page) on recalibrating a camera from the features it already sees, with no target, and on whether the solver's own uncertainty is honest enough for a robot to accept or reject the update. Milestone 1 uses OpenCV's real stereo calibration photos (two cameras, 13 views each, Apache-2.0): the checkerboard corners are kept as correspondences but the board's geometry is withheld, so the 54 corners become free 3-D points. Started 30% off in focal length, bundle adjustment lands at 534.8 and 538.4 px against Zhang's 535.6 and 539.7 px (gaps 0.15% and 0.24%, under 1σ), with a reported σ 1.12× Zhang's, refuting our prediction of a 2× price for having no target. The free corners leave their best plane by 0.0077 square widths rms (0.024 at most), and the two cameras, solved separately, reconstruct the same bend (correlation 0.90; 0.91 with a second distortion term): the printed board is not flat, which a flat-board model cannot absorb (target-free reprojection error 0.26 against 0.30 px per coordinate). Over 400 random subsets of 3 to 12 views the focal length's z-score against the all-view reference has rms 1.94 (95% 1.75–2.12) for 4–12 views, so the reported σ is about twice too small; Zhang's is no better (2.16). Limits: one rig and board, corners without mismatches, the reference is itself a flat-board fit, and every solve stopped on its evaluation cap. Milestone 2 fixes the solver (gauge pinned, analytic Jacobian, Levenberg–Marquardt: all 560 solves converge, at most 177 evaluations) and confirms milestone 1's rms z (1.945 against 1.944). The largest angle between the views' board normals predicts the focal error (Spearman ρ −0.46 and −0.58), and the reported σ tracks it (ρ +0.39 / +0.45) but stays about 2× too small, 2.4× on 160 near-critical subsets of near-parallel boards. There Zhang's σ is much worse (rms z 5.8) and its focal length is further off (median 1.50% against 1.09% at 4 views). A pre-registered accept gate, σf/f ≤ 0.5%, rejected 92% of updates more than 2% off but accepted only 84% of those within 1%, short of the 90/90 target; an inflation factor fitted on one camera did not transfer cleanly to the other. Milestone 3 asks whether the 2× is real and whether a robust σ fixes it. Scored against the target-free all-view solution with the nested variance, rms z is still 2.28, so the checkerboard reference is not the cause. A leave-one-view-out jackknife (3,480 re-solves) gives an honest σ with no fitted factor: rms z 0.70 and 0.65, 2σ coverage 97–99%, and 1.01 on near-critical subsets where the reported σ gives 2.34; the cluster-robust sandwich helps only on one camera. But the jackknife is very conservative at 4 views (15× the reported σ) and ranks good against bad updates worse (ROC AUC 0.75 against 0.91), so a 0.5% jackknife gate accepts only 19% of good updates: an honest error bar and a good accept statistic are different things. Milestone 5 tests the two suspects milestone 1 named. OpenCV's released-object calibration (a bend-aware Zhang) turns out to be the same estimator as the target-free bundle adjustment: identical intrinsics, σ and board shape to 1e-6 px, because free corners leave the board only its scale. Against it, the flat, evenly spaced board assumption alone moves the principal point cy by 8.7 px (left) and 5.3 px (right) while reporting a 1 px σ. A second radial term k2 is clearly non-zero but does not make σ honest: nested rms z 3.01 (2.00 without five outliers) against 2.28 with k1 alone. Residuals of neighbouring corners stay correlated (0.31 and 0.24), but only along one board axis (0.44–0.56, against about 0 along the other), which points at the board or the detector rather than the lens. Milestone 1's reprojection comparison was corrected here (0.30 against 0.26 px per coordinate, not 0.42 against 0.26). Milestone 6 traces the one-axis residual pattern to the corner localiser used so far: cornerSubPix with an 11×11 half-window (a 23 px box) misplaces corners on the board's outer ring by up to 6.4 px, because the box runs off the pattern. All 26 corners that differ by more than 1 px from a 5×5 window are on that ring. With a 5×5 window or OpenCV's findChessboardCornersSB, reprojection error halves and the one-directional structure mostly goes. This corrects milestone 5: the flat-board shift of cy is 1.2 px (left) and 1.4 px (right) with SB corners, not 8.7 and 5.3; the bend survives, 25–45% shallower and still seen identically by both cameras. The localiser alone moves Zhang's focal length by up to 7.2 px (1.3%), several times any reported σ. And cleaner corners make the reported σ less honest, not more: it halves while the error barely moves, so the nested rms z rises from 2.28 to 3.1–3.5. A sandwich σ clustered by board column does not help (2.44 / 1.72). The four pre-registered hypotheses: one held, three refuted.
